title: Make Believe Ballroom and Melody Parade
summary: They sort out the 1949 Make Believe Ballroom film, Martin Block versus Al Jarvis, and the Universal featurette Melody Parade with the Pied Pipers.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: Yeah. The merger came way later. "Make Believe Ballroom," 1949, directed by Joseph Sandley. Routine musical but rich in jazz appearances. Jimmy Dorsey and His Orchestra. Pee Wee Hunt and His Band. Charlie Barnet and His Band. Gene Krupa and His Band. And the King Cole Trio.
Well, I remember the picture, but I can't remember anything about it.
Was that Al Jarvis's Make Believe Ballroom, or Martin Block's? Probably Al Jarvis's, wasn't it?
What was the date on that?

I would be inclined to think that Martin Block had arrested the supremacy of the battle of the Make Believe Ballrooms by then. I think more people associated -- around the country associated Martin with that than Al.
Yeah, I think so, too, although Al was -- Martin was still on the air. Did he still call it that in --
Well, remember he came out here and did it out here.
Yeah, yeah. I remember I met him in

New York in '49. "Melody Parade," 1944, directed by Lewis D. Collins. Universal Music featurette, 15 minutes. Spotlighting Charlie Barnet and His Orchestra and a stage setting, entertaining, with support from the Pied Pipers, June Hutton -- well, June Hutton would be in the Pied Pipers, right? Dorothy Allen, Gray and Diane, and Kay Starr. Numbers included, "How Am I to Know," "Redskin Rhumba," "Skyliner," -- it wasn't Les Cowan -- and "Washington Whirligig."
Yeah.
Remember that?
Well, I assure you Will Cowan was around there someplace.
Well, it was at Universal.
Well, he probably produced it.
Oh, all right. I mean if it was "Skyliner," and it was Universal, it was Will Cowan.
Yes, sir.
But June Hutton would have been singing with the Pied Pipers, wouldn't she? Yeah, she would have been.
I don't think so. She never sang with the Pied Pipers, did she?
Oh, yes. Yeah. Not back in the Dorsey days, but later, when the Pied Pipers were an independent musical group, and with Frank Sinatra. He had them singing
with him on his radio show in 1944.
Was this '44?
Uh-huh. I think that's what it says. '44, yeah. Yeah, they were singing, Clark Yokum, Hal Hopper and one other, and June Hutton, were the Pied Pipers, during those years.
I wasn't aware that June had ever been with the Pied Pipers.
